73a55a682600a5a82a855c95313b8d7152df065b.summary: Halcyon RISE Team report (published 2025-07-02) says cybercriminals, including Scattered Spider, compromise call centers and other business process outsourcing (BPO) providers to reach many victims, often in a few sectors. It cites insider recruitment, social engineering, removal of global administrators in Azure tenants, BYOVD and EDR evasion, data-first extortion, and ransomware such as Akira, Play, Qilin and DragonForce. It includes mitigation advice for defenders.

hedges: Attacks against UK retail and US insurance industries likely originated, at least in part, from the group's compromise of BPO companies.
The phase-by-phase attack lifecycle is described as suspected.
Initial access would likely have included credential phishing; callback phishing 'may have been used' to reinforce trust.
The threat actors likely enrolled new MFA tokens to maintain persistent access.
The group has been linked to multiple ransomware payloads.
Scattered Spider appears to favor Conti-based encryptors.
Organizations should assume Scattered Spider or similar actors may already be present in outsourced environments.

73bcdf2f6319054ffaebeea727782259e9870d60.summary: CrowdStrike Threat Intel report on the May 2021 Colonial Pipeline ransomware incident, which was likely caused by a DarkSide affiliate. CrowdStrike links DarkSide to CARBON SPIDER and judges the group highly likely Russia-based. The report describes RaaS operators and underground forums restricting ransomware activity and moving to private channels, and access brokers targeting energy-sector firms. It expects CARBON SPIDER to stay active, possibly under a new brand.
